items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: Actually it was Sharky's band at that time.

ctx.x: What difference did he make when he played? But, it is a funny thing about trombone, because how many bands had trombones when you were there?

Well, of course, I was there doing a depressed era. And there were very few trombones being used, except in the big spot job in bands. They always used trombone in full sections, but the little joints, they just dropped trombone. That's it. They used trumpet, clarinet, dubbing sax, and bass, drums, and piano. For example, Freddie Newman's band at the Silver Slipper consisted of Sharky. Actually it was Sharky's band at that time. Freddie Newman was playing piano, Ching Martin was playing bass, Mark Hazel was…

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: Sharky was playing Silver Slipper and had a little band at the Studio Club with Pat De Queer. And, that was where I posed in and numerous other guys.

ctx.x: Just so I can see what's happening here. I'm trying to figure out how to prop it out. That's okay. Go ahead. It's facing you.

Okay. There was a music store in 3-4th, formed by Bubba Broyles. Bubba was a trumpet player, and he'd been playing with the local bands there. And, he was a great friend of Mr. A.J. LaCoste, who was a power with the Whirland Organization. A.J. was the management of the band department. He organized school bands all over Mississippi and Louisiana. He was a tremendous man. But, Bubba and LaCoste asked me to come to New Orleans, that I would have some kind of a job. I had, I tried to go back to playing and played…
You have to be careful. Now you were talking about Leslie Nurse, was his name?
